notes.title: Relentless Frontier: The Big Roadmap
notes.notes:
What it do, fellow humans? Korzodin here, project lead for Relentless Frontier! Hope you've all remained alive and hydrated in these [i]thrilling[/i] times.

Us? We've been plugging away at Relentless Frontier, progressing along the Big Roadmap. [i]"What is the Big Roadmap?"[/i] you ask? Let me show you:

[h1]LORE N' VANIA UPDATE[/h1]
[h3]Planned Release: Q3 2025[/h3]

Lore N' Vania! A sorta goofy way to say:

[b]We're adding more lore and story to Episode 1, as well as improving the exploration aspect.[/b] 

Story and Exploration are the two primary focuses of this update, but we've got a whole list of planned improvements:

[list]
[*][b]Lore[/b] - We're improving the game setting through data logs and environmental storytelling. The city maps, in particular, have received a lot of work.
[*][b]Vania[/b] - We're leaning more into the Metroidvania aspects of Relentless Frontier, adding more environmental interactivity with the abilities the player acquires. 
[*][b]The Pulverizer[/b] - A new bolt-action mine thrower! Launches sticky proximity mines that can latch onto the environment as a trap, or fired directly at the enemy to detonate on impact. Effective against armor and swarms, but the ammo is rare and expensive to omnistruct. Use 'em wisely!
[*][b]Poison Pods[/b] - The bugs have started using chemical warfare! These armored, purple-glowing pods emit a potent corrosive gas, eating through armor and flesh alike in the blink of an eye. Direct damage doesn't seem to have an effect, but they seem to be extremely flammable...
[*][b]An Actual Ending Sequence[/b] - You will no longer be dumped into a "YOURE WINNER" screen at the end of Episode 1!
[*][b]Improved FX[/b] - Better gore, more destructibility, cooler hit feedback, and most importantly, etc! Lots and lots of etc.
[*][b]UI / UX Improvements[/b] - Smoothing out the menus, and adding more options (Including a walk/run toggle!)
[*][b]Bombardier Refinements[/b] - Everyone's favorite lump of literal (and metaphorical) bugginess is getting some much-needed attention! We want to emphasize his role as an artillery tank, and make him less frustrating to fight without fire damage. Maybe get him a new coat of FX work?
[/list]

[h1]GOING ROGUE UPDATE[/h1]
[h3]Planned Release: Early 2026 (rough estimate)[/h3]

 [i]Not quite going full rogue, just going more rogue-like... [/i]

The "Going Rogue" update will add a new game mode: Rogue Mode. This mode will add a variety of randomization and progression options for a customized second/third/hundredth playthrough!

A [b]few[/b] of our plans for this mode include:

[list]
[*] New Upgrades - The likes of which would have made the base campaign horribly imbalanced! But in Rogue Mode, the sky's the limit (sometimes literally, with the right mobility upgrades).
[*] Random Events - Maybe you come across a squad of friendly RDI troops, maybe you find a drop pod filled with supplies or upgrades, or maybe a pack of Titans decide to show up and ruin your day? Who knows, roll the dice!
[*] Enemy Mutations - Enemies can spawn with random mutations, giving them extra abilities and effects! 
[*] Corruption Cards - At the start of every level, choose one of three gameplay modifiers to add to the rest of the run!
[*] Endless Mode - Run doesn't end until you die. Levels are shuffled, and once you beat a set, they're shuffled again. Get them massive gains / corrupt your run to insanity!
[/list]

[h1]EPISODE 2[/h1]
[h3]Planned Release: 2026 (rough estimate)[/h3]

I'm going to be real with you guys for a moment -

Episode 2 is a doozy. We're introducing new enemy factions, a large hub-connected environment, and a [i]bunch[/i] of new mechanics and weapons.

The biggest reason for Episode 2's doozy-ness: [b]we've decided to combine Episodes 2 and 3[/b]. I wanna make this clear, [i]you're not losing content.[/i] We didn't want player progression to get interrupted for this episode, as it's going to be a much larger factor in Episode 2. Pacing-wise, it will feel much better as one part. Story-wise, it will be much more impactful.

All that being said - I'm [i]very[/i] excited for Episode 2. Maybe I'm a bit biased? But I'm hoping that excitement comes through in a tangible way.

- Michael "Korzodin" Ewer

notes.title: Relentless Frontier Update 0.5.0 Now Available
notes.notes:
Heyo! We've got a new major update for Relentless Frontier and a Soundtrack release, dropped just in time for the Steam Winter Sale! What a coincidence!

Update Changes include:
[list]
[*]New Score Attack Gamemode! Start fully-equipped with extra lives and DO BIG COMBO to watch that score sail and get those letter grade medallions!*
[*]Improved Shotgun Altfire! The electrodart affects more enemies, creates a huge electric explosion when it hits water, and can supercharge explosive barrels, launch flame canisters, and turn the electric barrel into an electric turret!
[*] A bunch of bugfixes and improvements!
[/list]

Also, take a look and a listen at the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3236860/Relentless_Frontier_Soundtrack/]Relentless Frontier Soundtrack![/url] Good jams cooked-up by Malaphors and John S. Weekly (Primeval)! High quality FLACS and additional suite mixes are part of the deal!

Hope everyone enjoys the rest of their year!

notes.title: Relentless Frontier Update 0.4.2 Now Available
notes.notes:
Top of the [TIME UNIT] to ya. We've been toiling in the dev mines to drag up some raw IMPROVEMENTS to Relentless Frontier, and I think we've got some good stuff to show just before Boomstock! 

Main Changes:
[list]
[*] Level Select has been added! When you start a new game, you can either start up a campaign like normal, or go to Level Select and choose which level you would like to start on (as long as you've been to the level once before), as well as the difficulty.
[*] Menu Upgrade! We've done some work on the main menu, and laid down some framework for the extra game modes we have planned for the future.
[*] Aim Assist! We've implemented an enhanced aim assist (thanks Jay!). Can be toggled in the Gameplay settings, with adjustable pull strength.
[*] Finished optimization on all enemy sprites, which has lowered VRAM usage a bit more. Should result in better performance when a bunch of enemies are shooting and spitting and clawing and whatnot.
[*] A buncha small map changes and fixes!
[/list]

Next update, we'll be adding some new side areas to Episode 1, beefing up the story a bit, and adding the Score Attack gameplay mutator! (Score attack is fun as hell btw, can't wait to show it off).

As always, if you've got feedback or questions, let us know!

notes.title: Relentless Frontier 0.4.1 now available on Beta Branch
notes.notes:
Heyo! We heard your complaints and have been hard at work fixing (some of) them!

Main changes:
[list]
[*]Optimized Titan sprites to take up less VRAM. This brings the game below the 8gm VRAM mark with all assets loaded, which should help with frame issues on mid / high-tier computers. We're looking to optimize more sprites this way in the coming months.
[*]E1M6 split into two maps! E1M6 was pretty huge, which unfortunately put a lot of strain on peoples computers (and especially Steam Decks!). Splitting the map has lowered load times and increased gameplay performance a bunch.
[*]Gunner Slugs sprites have been changed, to make them stick out a bit better. Hopefully they don't get confused for their dumber, punchier cousins as often.
[*]Relentless difficulty rebalanced! Its a lot harder now. Sorry?
[*]General monster placement rebalanced a bit. You might be surprised with what you find on E1M2 and E1M3...
[/list]

There's a bunch of other stuff, I'll have a more organized list of every change we have logged later down the line. It's mostly bug fixes and little adjustments to make the game feel better. Of course, if you find any bugs or issues, let us know on the Steam Forums or in our [url=http://discord.gg/fp59DpxEkV]Discord![/url]

[h2]IMPORTANT[/h2]
[b]Changing versions is very likely to break your saves.[/b] Be ready to start a new game if you switch to the beta branch!

notes.title: Confirmation of Release Date: July 24th
notes.notes:
This is a just a quick message confirming that the release date for Relentless Frontier early access is [b]July 24th[/b]. We announced the shifting of the date over a week ago, but very cleverly forgot to mention it on Steam. 

The reason for the delay is the usual stuff, we found a few (non flammable) bugs that were serious enough to warrant another week of polish and testing to make sure Relentless Frontier is fit for release. And the good news is that it is! The issues found have been fixed and we're very much in the final stages of being ready to share this with you all. There will be a proper release day new post with all the juicy details so I'll leave it at that. 

On behalf of the Relentless Frontier team, 

Cheers,

BB

notes.title: Whoops, All Crystals!
notes.notes:
Hey everybody! RF Project Lead Korzodin here, with some progress on a horror-themed map! I also bring news about the Early Access release date, new ways you can stalk me while I work on RF, and some additional planned features that I'm pretty sure some of you will appreciate! Let's get down to it:


[h2]E1M7: Surge Protection[/h2]

Noah finds his way to the Blackwater Power Plant, a massive underground geothermal / nuclear power plant with it's own crystal mine. He's on the trail of the city governor, who carries an important key and chose to flee to the mines and probably die in a really inconvenient spot. What a jerk!

It's fine. Noah is armed to the teeth. The lights are out and the power is failing, but the darkness isn't hiding anything he can't handle... right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40887254/3372d183389f1c586d46182f8804d549ea0cf4db.png[/img]

Theatrics aside, horror is hard to design when the player can move at the speed of light and dump out damage at a similar rate! We had to get psychological, and come up with with a concept completely foreign to the player; [strike]enemy variety[/strike] [i]something the player doesn't want to shoot.[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40887254/53e76ddfdc79c82abb3c6e2ff57f9566f689f371.png[/img]

Also, crystals and mushrooms! They radiate light, and other things that might cause some long-term problems. Don't worry about it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40887254/b1727af2874b116c281e128ac80de0f3aaef8a9a.png[/img]


[h2]Early Access Release Date[/h2]

Gonna just rip the bandage off quick here, we've chosen to delay the Early Access release date. We were rushing, we were making mistakes, we wouldn't have enough time for testing. I know Early Access likely has some expectations of roughness, but I want to make damn sure that what we release to the public is stable and fun. 

We definitely still plan to release EA this year. We'll announce a solid date once we're feature complete and testing. 


[h2]Dev Streams[/h2]

I stream Relentless Frontier development on Twitch! Check it out:
https://www.twitch.tv/korzodin_rf


Whenever I do level design, sound design, or graphic design, I stream my work on Twitch. I've been streaming for a couple of weeks now, and I think I've got this "streamer" thing figured out. I typically stream on weekdays, from 6 - 10pm PST. Drop in and say hi!


[h2]Discord Server[/h2]

We have a Discord server! Join up here:
discord.gg/fp59DpxEkV


I post rougher progress shots here, and I'm pretty open to any questions or discussion. Again, drop in and say hi!


[h2]Future Plans[/h2]

A quick list of planned features (that will probably be in our next progress post):
[list]
[*] [b]Toggle-able weapon upgrades![/b] When you get a weapon upgrade, you can toggle it on/off to suit your needs. Some upgrades have added power/utility with an added cost or some other side effects, so we figured being able to toggle these would be pretty helpful.
[*] [b]Interactive Data Logs![/b] If you're curious about what's been happening on Ross 128b while Noah was away, you can get some extra lore by reading tablets, computers, TV screens, etc. Some of this stuff might also hint at secrets and alternate routes! Alternatively, you can totally ignore these and just shoot stuff and jump around! You don't need to read any of these to progress.
[*] [b]Voice Acting![/b] Yes, we're still planning on having our main cast voiced! We've got some VAs in mind, but if you're interested in pretending to be murdered in a recording, let us know! (DM me on discord, twitter, steam, etc)
[/list]

Anything else you're interested in knowing? Ask in the comments!

Peace,
- Korzodin

notes.title: Nextfest Demo Update
notes.notes:
Hey Everybody! We actually released this build a few weeks ago, but we kept it hush-hush until Nextfest started. Here's a truncated list of changes this build:

- New Enemy, the Missile Drone! They try to keep their distance and barrage the player with missiles. Just keep moving, and maybe try to lure some other enemies into the blast zone?
- New Weapon Upgrade, the Shredder Shot! An upgrade for the Peacekeeper Shotgun that gives it's pellets the ability to pierce soft targets and bounce off of the environment. Excellent for clearing hallways and caves!
- Newly remastered music by the powerful composer team Malaphors! 
- Improved drone enemy AI
- Improved enemy hit feedback, including impact sounds and more gore!
- Updated Omnifuel HUD
- Lots of optimization work
- A bunch of boring stuff that makes the game play better, I promise!

Give it a go, and let us know what it was like! We're always looking for feedback, and we love hearing about how your playthroughs went.

notes.title: Steam Demo V1.1
notes.notes:
After some feedback and an additional round of testing, we've made some fixes and improvements to the Relentless Frontier demo build! Not too many bugs (ironically), but we definitely had plenty of feedback regarding difficulty. Let us know what you think!

Changelog V1.1:

[list]
[*] The Guardian's leap attack can now be reliably countered by the shotgun! Try it out for yourself, you can blast them out of the air if you react quick enough to them jumping up to wherever you are.
[*] Lowered Slug movement speed on Easy and Medium, and increased it on Relentless. Hopefully cuts down on players getting unfairly overwhelmed.
[*] Omniaxe melee range increased slightly, and the first swing with the Omniaxe when it's actually equipped now affects the correct areas. Melee still does the same amount of damage, but the increased area of effect should make the melee a more viable defensive option vs slugs.
[*] Ambient light levels increased in the secret Peacekeeper upgrade encounter cave. This fight should still be very difficult, but not through blinding the player.
[*] Additional blood added to Slug deaths.
[*] Fixed wacky scrolling cement texture in E1M2 aqueduct encounter room.
[*] Fixed the S.H.E.W.P. lifebar, should behave correctly after loading a save now.
[*] Fixed portal behavior in the flickering rust hallway after the Peacekeeper upgrade arena.
[*] Removed the "Reset to Defaults" option in the menu until the defaults can properly be defined. This was restoring the wrong defaults, and messing up a lot of things behind the scenes.
[*] Fixed the FOV slider, now shows the correct field title, the min/max values were changed to 60/150, and  the value increment was changed from 0.1 to 1.
[*] Combined the Advanced Sound submenu with the basic Sound menu.
[*] Midi device option removed (There are no midis. Yet.)
[*] Altered Beta Noire drone spawn rate on Relentless. They shouldn't get stuck on each other anymore.
[*] Increased size of Guardian armor hitsparks for visual clarity.
[*] Added autosave after the Beta Noire fight on E1M4.
[*] Moved Omnitank away from the vent grating in E1M2 waterway secret. Player can no longer grab it from the other side of the grating.
[*] The orange nest goop's friction was decreased from 0.75 to 0.85, slows the same as mud now.
[*] Default value for all volume set to 30%, to avoid blowing out new player's ears on startup.
[*] Indestructible wire spool added to E1M2 scanner secret to avoid softlocks.
[/list]
